body.statement: Under the fixed interior probabilities \(r_{\ell j,n}=p^{\circ}_{\ell j}\in[\varepsilon_{\rm int},1-\varepsilon_{\rm int}]\), mutually independent Bernoulli role observations, and \(n_{\ell j}/n\to\pi_{\ell j}>0\), the outcome-independent sixty-role split satisfies, jointly over \(1\le\ell\le L\), \[\sqrt n(\widehat\Delta^E_{\ell}-\Delta_{\ell})=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{j=1}^{4}\sum_{a=1}^{n_{\ell j}}\iota^{\circ}_{\ell j}(E_{\ell j a,n})+o_{P}(1)\;\Rightarrow\;N(0,\Omega^{\circ}_{\ell}),\] with independent coordinates, where \(\iota^{\circ}_{\ell j}(e)=\gamma^{\circ}_{\ell j}(e-p^{\circ}_{\ell j})/\pi_{\ell j}\), \(\gamma^{\circ}_{\ell1}=\phi(v^{\circ}_{\ell})/\phi(q(p^{\circ}_{\ell1}))\), \(\gamma^{\circ}_{\ell2}=\phi(v^{\circ}_{\ell})/\phi(q(p^{\circ}_{\ell2}))\), \(\gamma^{\circ}_{\ell3}=-\phi(v^{\circ}_{\ell})/\phi(q(p^{\circ}_{\ell3}))\), \(\gamma^{\circ}_{\ell4}=-1\), \(v^{\circ}_{\ell}=q(p^{\circ}_{\ell1})+q(p^{\circ}_{\ell2})-q(p^{\circ}_{\ell3})\), and \(\Omega^{\circ}_{\ell}=\sum_{j=1}^{4}(\gamma^{\circ}_{\ell j})^2p^{\circ}_{\ell j}(1-p^{\circ}_{\ell j})/\pi_{\ell j}\). Consequently, \(\sqrt n\{L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\widehat\Delta^E_{\ell}-\overline\Delta\}\Rightarrow N(0,L^{-2}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\Omega^{\circ}_{\ell})\). The interior margin is exactly the finite-threshold standard-normal specialization of Djuazon and Tsyawo's Assumption 5; the independent blocks and positive role shares specialize their sampling and dominance conditions; and \(\gamma^{\circ}\) is the gradient in their proof equation (S.3), with the treated-post term added as in Theorem 2(c). Thus this split-sample result is a direct fixed-threshold specialization of their Theorem 2, not a novelty-bearing extension.
body.justification: The explicit normalization and influence function show exactly how the outcome-independent role split changes information while preserving the published interior DTT limit.
body.gap: Djuazon and Tsyawo's Theorem 2 already supplies the general interior Gaussian result; this proposition is its finite-threshold, disjoint-role specialization and asserts no tightening.
body.consumer: Practitioners can switch to the published interior Gaussian interpretation when all sixty role probabilities remain uniformly away from zero.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\ell\) and write \(p_j=p^\circ_{\ell j}\).  The interior margin places \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_4)\) in a compact subset of \((0,1)^4\), on which the exact-link map
\[
g(p)=H(p_1,p_2,p_3)-p_4
\]
is twice continuously differentiable with bounded Hessian.  With
\(
v=q(p_1)+q(p_2)-q(p_3),
\)
direct differentiation gives
\[
\nabla g(p)=\left(
\frac{\phi(v)}{\phi(q(p_1))},
\frac{\phi(v)}{\phi(q(p_2))},
-\frac{\phi(v)}{\phi(q(p_3))},
-1\right)=\gamma^\circ_\ell.
\tag{1}
\]
The add-half identity
\[
\widetilde r_j-p_j
=\frac{K_j-n_jp_j}{n_j+1}+\frac{1/2-p_j}{n_j+1}
\tag{2}
\]
shows that the deterministic smoothing term is \(O(n^{-1})=o(n^{-1/2})\).  Taylor expansion of \(g\), using the bounded Hessian and \(\widetilde r-p=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), then gives
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\Delta^E_\ell-\Delta_\ell\}
=\sum_{j=1}^4\gamma^\circ_{\ell j}
\frac{\sqrt n}{n_{\ell j}+1}
\sum_{a=1}^{n_{\ell j}}(E_{\ell ja,n}-p^\circ_{\ell j})+o_P(1).
\]
Because \(n_{\ell j}/n\to\pi_{\ell j}>0\), replacing \(\sqrt n/(n_{\ell j}+1)\) by \(1/(\sqrt n\,\pi_{\ell j})\) changes the expression by \(o_P(1)\).  This proves the asserted linear representation with
\[
\iota^\circ_{\ell j}(e)=\frac{\gamma^\circ_{\ell j}}{\pi_{\ell j}}
(e-p^\circ_{\ell j}).
\]
For clarity, the characteristic function of the resulting centered sum has logarithm
\[
-\frac{t^2}{2}\sum_{j=1}^4
\frac{(\gamma^\circ_{\ell j})^2p^\circ_{\ell j}(1-p^\circ_{\ell j})}{\pi_{\ell j}}+o(1),
\]
because its maximal summand is \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  It therefore converges to \(N(0,\Omega^\circ_\ell)\).  Mutual independence of all role observations gives independent limits across the fixed pairs.  Averaging the linear representations yields
\[
\sqrt n\left\{L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\widehat\Delta^E_\ell-\overline\Delta\right\}
\Rightarrow N\!\left(0,L^{-2}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\Omega^\circ_\ell\right).
\]
Finally, the identification proof shows that splitting does not change the population DTT functional.  The displayed interior margin, positive limiting shares, and gradient (1) are precisely the fixed-threshold standard-normal specializations named in the benchmark assumptions; the treated-post derivative is the additional \(-1\) component.  Thus the mathematical limit is the stated split-role specialization and does not assert a boundary extension of the published interior theorem.
